text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has said a constitutional amendment bill was being prepared to control sectarianism, purge society of heinous crimes and improve law and order.
- Ten passengers were killed and seven others sustained injuries in a road accident near Faizabad village some 130 kilometeres from Larkana on Thursday night.
- The wheat flour supply has been stabilised to a major extent, the government says it received no complaint of shortages on Friday.
- Former chairman of Oil and Gas Development Corporation Riffat Askari died of heart failure during judicial custody.

- China continues to ship M-11 missile components to Pakistan despite pledges made in 1994 not to do so, a senior U.S. State Department official said on Thursday while testifying before a Senate sub-committee.
- The government is considering introducing a law for compulsory screening for AIDS, Hepatitis-B, Hepatitis-C, malaria and syphills, sources said.
- The government is considering suspension of 325 officials accused of corruption.
- The hopes of keeping country's trade deficit below three billion dollars seem to have petered out as the exports lagged imports $2.6 billion during the last three quarters.
- Federal Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz expects to receive an encouraging response from tax payers within six months following recent tax cuts made in their favour.
- The revised tariff rates of customs duties announced in economic revival package on March 28 reduced duties from 13 to 5 percent.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar has said that 90 percent of anomalies in the economic package had been removed.
